national_news.title: India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement Comes into Force
bullets: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force, providing duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand.
Both nations agreed to work towards doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to approximately ₹35,000 crore by 2030.
Sensitive sectors like dairy remain protected, while New Zealand committed to facilitate USD 20 billion in investments into India.

national_news.title: India Records Over $748 Billion in FDI Inflows Between 2014 and 2025
bullets: India received a record over USD 748 billion in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) between 2014 and 2025, with source countries rising from 89 to 112.
The government liberalized sectoral norms, permitting up to 74% FDI in defense and 100% in telecom, insurance, and space sectors.
Key reforms aim to create an investor-friendly environment and position India as a preferred global investment destination in alignment with Viksit Bharat 2047.

national_news.title: President Murmu Congratulates Indian Medalists at Asian Para Games 2026
bullets: President Droupadi Murmu congratulated Indian athletes including Rinku (Gold) and Ajeet Singh (Silver) in the Men's Javelin F46 event at the Asian Para Games 2026.
Mona Agarwal won Gold and Avani Lekhara won Silver in the Women's 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event, with Agarwal setting a new Asian Para Games record.
Other medalists congratulated include Soumya and Radha Venkatesh (Athletics), Nishad Kumar (Long Jump), Ravi K. Budigina (Swimming), and Kokila and Kapil Parmar (Judo).

national_news.title: Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar Conferred on 106 Young Artists
bullets: Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat conferred the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for 2024 and 2025 upon 106 young artists in New Delhi.
Presented by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the award recognizes outstanding talent among young practitioners in the field of performing arts.
Notable awardees include Manisha Srivastava (Bihar) for Folk Music, Akram Khan Behrupiya (Rajasthan) for Folk Dance, Hito Kiho (Nagaland) for Choir Music, and Subhashree Swain for Chhau Dance.

national_news.title: Charles Matata Breaks Course Record at Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon
bullets: Kenya’s Charles Matata won the men’s elite race at the Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon, breaking the course record with a time of 58 minutes and 52 seconds over the 21.097-km course.
Ethiopia’s Wudinesh Alemu claimed the women’s elite title finishing in 1 hour, 6 minutes, and 35 seconds.
In the Indian elite category, Shailesh Kushwaha won the men’s race in 1:05:05, while Ankita Dhyani secured the women’s title in 1:12:46.
